name: View Royal

facts.text: View Royal's Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1069 protects Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood, Pacific yew, Douglas-fir, grand fir and bigleaf maple. Shore pine was added in the 2022 update.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Protection Bylaw | Town of View Royal
facts.excerpt: Shore Pine has been added as a protected species
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: In View Royal any tree over 30 cm in diameter is protected, measured 1.3 m above the highest ground at the trunk.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Protection Bylaw | Town of View Royal
facts.excerpt: any tree having a diameter greater than 30cm D.B.H.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: View Royal requires a tree permit to remove or alter a protected tree. The 2024 application form points to section 5.3.2 of Bylaw 1069.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Removal or Alterations | Town of View Royal
facts.excerpt: Tree Permits are required for the removal or alteration of trees designated as a Protected Tree
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: View Royal requires a 15 m setback for buildings and structures from freshwater streams and from the shorelines of Esquimalt Harbour, Portage Inlet and the Millstream and Craigflower creek estuaries.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Regulations | Town of View Royal
facts.excerpt: 15m required setback for buildings and structures from the natural boundary of freshwater streams and the shoreline of Esquimalt Harbour, Portage Inlet
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Work near protected watercourses in View Royal falls in a Natural Watercourse and Shoreline Areas Development Permit Area. It may need a Riparian Area Assessment under the provincial regulation.
facts.sourceTitle: Development Permits | Town of View Royal
facts.excerpt: may require a Riparian Area Assessment, in compliance with the Provincial Riparian Areas Protection Regulation

facts.text: Parts of View Royal sit in a wildland-urban interface beside Thetis Lake and Mill Hill regional parks, where a wildfire burned in July 2020. Homes near Thetis Lake are priority areas for fuel reduction.
facts.sourceTitle: View Royal Strata Becomes First FireSmart Recognized Neighbourhood in Greater Victoria (Town of View Royal, 2026)
facts.excerpt: an area that has experienced wildfire in the past, including the Mill Hill wildfire in July 2020
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: View Royal Fire offers free FireSmart home assessments (firesmart@viewroyal.ca, 250-479-7322) and links to FireSmart landscaping guides. That makes plant choice and clearance around the house a real local concern.
facts.excerpt: contact View Royal FireSmart at firesmart@viewroyal.ca or call 250-479-7322 to book your FREE assessment

facts.text: In February 2026 the 43-unit Stonecliffe townhome strata near Mill Hill became the first FireSmart-recognised neighbourhood in Greater Victoria, after resident clean-up projects.
facts.sourceTitle: View Royal Strata Becomes First FireSmart Recognized Neighbourhood in Greater Victoria (Town of View Royal, 2026)

facts.text: Regional (CRD, not municipal): from May 1 to September 30, lawns on the regional water supply may be watered two days a week by address (even: Wednesday and Saturday; odd: Thursday and Sunday). The day limits apply only to lawns.
facts.excerpt: The watering schedule days only apply to lawns!
